Subject: EEAS DELEGATIONS PRESS REVIEW - MOLDOVA - 28 September 2023



 

Daily Press Review

28 September 2023 

EU Delegation Moldova


 
POLITICAL NEWS

 

The explosive part of a rocket that fell into the lake in Harbova , Anenii Noi, was detonated

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

Specialists from Bombteh detonated the explosive component of a rocket that fell into the lake in Harbova village, Anenii Noi district, about 60 kilometres from Chisinau. In order for the intervention to be operated safely, the specialists evacuated the water from the lake. The authorities have confirmed that the debris come from an aerial missile, and specialists will identify its type and origin. The MAI states that there was no danger to the population. The area was isolated, and the first houses are located at a distance of one kilometre. Few days earlier, fragments of a rocket fell in the village of Chitcani in Causeni district.



Spinu: A mayor who is against the EU is a mayor who acts against the development of his locality

Source: realitatea.md

Andrei Spinu, Minister for Infrastructure and Regional Development, asserted on Rlive TV's Rezoomat programme that a mayor against the European Union (EU) acts against their own locality's development. Spinu clarified that government-managed funds reach all localities, irrespective of the mayor's views. Spinu emphasised that without pre-accession or European funds, local development cannot be achieved. He pointed out that the EU will not finance Moldova if the country does not fulfil its EU accession action plans. Drawing on Romania, Bulgaria, and Croatia's experiences, he noted that once certain things are done, resources become available. This emphasises the importance of EU relations for local and national development.



The Revival Party's candidate for the position of Mayor of the capital, Vasile Bolea: connections with Shor, integration into the Customs Union and homophobic comments

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

Ahead of local elections, Vasile Bolea has left the Socialist Party and joined the Revival Party, which is under scrutiny for alleged illegal financing from oligarch Ilan Shor's organised crime group . Bolea, after announcing his candidacy for the position of Mayor of the capital, met with Russian Ambassador Oleg Vasne ov to discuss bilateral issues, regional trends, and local elections. The Revival Party plans to organise a referendum on Moldova's potential membership in the Eurasian Economic Union, Bolea explained. Previously, Bolea protested against the signing of the Association Agreement with the European Union. Meanwhile, the Socialist Party accused the Shor Party of attempting to corrupt socialist deputies and local elected officials in March 2023.


The new Minister of Finance has taken the oath of office

Source: voceabasarabiei.md

The designated Minister of Finance, Petru Rotaru, took the oath of office on 28 September. The ceremony took place in the presence of the President of the Republic of Moldova, Maia Sandu. The head of state thanked the former Minister of Finance, Veronica Sireteanu, who left office for maternal leave, for agreeing to take on "the responsibility of managing the Ministry of Finance in a difficult economic period ". Maia Sandu said that the new minister will lead the institution that oversees the good and prudent use of public money, our money of all, this being a responsible mission". The president also said that the experience of the new Minister of Finance, former head of Tax Office, is valuable for continuing efforts to reduce bureaucracy in the tax and customs fields.


Fugitive oligarch, sanctioned by the EU, filed a complaint against EU Council s decision

Source: jurnal.md

The oligarch Vladimir Plahotniuc, sanctioned in May by the Brussels authorities for attempts to destabilize the Republic of Moldova, sued the Council of the European Union. The case was registered on 9 August, but it was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 25 September. More specifically, Vladimir Plahotniuc requests the Court to cancel the decision regarding the establishment of restrictive measures against him and the annulment of the Regulation implementing the decision. The lawyer representing his interests in this case is Jason Pobjoy, specialized in European law, international law, public, commercial and competition law.


Websites of state institutions and of independent media were subjects to cyber attacks

Source: newsmaker.md

The spokesperson of the Government, Daniel Voda, has said that the websites of Chisinau airport, the energy regulator and the Foreign Ministry have been subjected to "massive DDoS attacks", but the relevant agency managed to minimise their impact. He explained that access to the websites from abroad "was temporarily limited to prevent their takeover". NewsMaker.md and a few other media, including the website of the Ziarul de Garda weekly and the Nokta website, as well as websites of several energy companies reported hacking attacks on 25-26 September.The Russian-language Telegram channel Narodnaya Cyber Armiya (People's Cyber Army) claimed responsibility for for these attacks.

 


ECONOMIC NEWS

 


Romania is interested in buying Moldovan Giurgiulesti international free port on Danube

Source: infotag.md


Romania is interested in buying the Giurgiulesti international free port from the Republic of Moldova. Romanian Prime Minister Marcel Ciolacu told Digi24.ro that the Romanian Minister of Transport has already discussed this topic with a representative of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the sole final owner of the company that manages the Danube port. Ciolacu mentioned that negotiations should not be conducted with the Moldovan authorities, since the shareholder of the Giurgiulesti port is the EBRD and, therefore, the negotiations will be conducted with the bank. Due to the war near the Moldovan border, the port of Giurgiulesti played a key role in the supply of goods to and from Ukraine, reaching a record cargo trans-shipment volume of 1.8 million tons in 2022. At the same time, 62% of goods exported through port were sent to the European Union. In this sense, a new berth is being built in the port of Giurgiulesti, to increase the trans-shipment of goods.

Andrei Spinu's promise: Moldova should get rid of Gazprom"

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

Andrei Spinu, Minister of Infrastructure and Regional Development, has promised to resume the repair of a key road to Tiraspol, left unfinished before the European Political Community summit at Bulboaca in June. Spinu discussed this shortly after launching an ambitious infrastructure reconstruction plan in Moldova, which he presents as a priority in his new term in the PAS government. He acknowledged that the authorities "had to ensure a good road up to the place" of the summit, and confirmed that work on the uncompleted section would resume in 2024 as part of a broader effort to rebuild the roads. Known for his role in solving the gas crisis from 2021-2022, Spinu told Free Europe that "Moldova must no longer have any relationship with Gazprom", the Russian state concern that was for a long time the only supplier of gas to Moldovan consumers.



Moldova's economy, hit by the crisis in 2023. EBRD adjusted the forecast for our country

Source: realitatea.md

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has adjusted its forecast for the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of Moldova for the current year, now anticipating zero economic growth rather than the previously predicted 1.3% decline. This announcement was made in the new regional economic analysis published in September. Meanwhile, the EBRD has maintained its economic growth forecast for Moldova in 2024, expecting the country's GDP to significantly increase by 3.5%. These adjustments follow an assessment of the economic situation in the first half of 2023, marking an improvement in recovery prospects. Despite a 2.4% decline in GDP in the first quarter of 2023, mainly due to the continuous decline in private consumption, there are signs of improvement.

 


FOREIGN POLICY

 


Ambassador: Attracting Chinese investments to Moldova is one of our priorities

Source: realitatea.md

China and Moldova are two friendly nations and great partners, always supporting each other in matters concerning sovereignty and territorial integrity, according to China's ambassador to Moldova, Yan Wenbin. In a speech marking the 74th anniversary of the proclamation of the People's Republic of China, Wenbin highlighted the strong desire to develop cooperation between the two countries in areas such as trade, investment, culture, and tourism. He emphasised that China's vast market is open to high-quality agricultural products from Moldova, and the Chinese Embassy is working to simplify the process for Moldovan sunflower and grape seeds to enter the Chinese market. Additionally, several memorandums of collaboration have been signed between universities in both countries.



Portugal will continue to support Moldova in the European integration process

Source: moldova1.md

Portugal will continue to support Moldova in its European integration process. This was discussed by Moldovan deputies Angela Munteanu-Pojoga and Iulia Dascalu and Portuguese parliamentarians. The officials also discussed trade and economic cooperation, legislative collaboration on anti-corruption measures, identifying and repatriating fraudulent assets, modernising energy infrastructure, and developing agriculture. The deputies also attended a concert organised by the Moldovan Cultural Centre in Portugal, marking its 20th anniversary, and presented the centre's leadership with certificates of high appreciation for their contribution to the Moldovan diaspora and their promotion of Moldovan culture and traditions.

 


EU-MOLDOVA RELATIONS

 


Roberta Metsola hopes that the EU will open accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova by the end of the year

Source: moldova1.md

President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola hopes that the EU will open accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova by year-end, asking for the hopes of these candidate countries not to be disappointed. Instead of focusing on a target date, Metsola stressed the importance of initiating accession negotiations by the end of the year. She has always shown her support for Ukraine's EU accession, even visiting Kyiv in April 2022 after the Russian invasion began. The EU granted Ukraine and Moldova candidate status in June 2022, although denied this to Georgia, calling for more reforms. The next step, opening accession negotiations, requires the fulfilment of seven benchmarks defined by the European Commission, mainly concerning widespread corruption and judicial reform.

 


HUMAN RIGHTS & JUSTICE

 


Olesea Stamate: The election of the Prosecutor General could take place in the new composition of the CSP

Source: moldova1.md

In a recent interview, Olesea Stamate, President of the Legal Commission within the Parliament of Moldova, discussed the dismissal of Prosecutor General Alexandr Stoianoglo, currently under criminal investigation, by presidential decree. She also examined the corruption allegations against Iulian Muntean, who has requested withdrawal from the Superior Council of Magistracy. Stamate emphasised the importance of a fair and efficient justice system and advocated for a new contest to fill the General Prosecutor position, organised by the Superior Council of Prosecutors. The interview delved into the Pre-Vetting process, designed to ensure integrity within the judiciary, and the impact of recent scandals on its reputation.



Where did the justice reform end up on the way of Moldova towards the accession negotiations

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

With just over two months until Brussels' decision on the prospect of opening Moldova's EU accession negotiations, up to 80% of justice commitments, six out of nine, have been fulfilled, according to Ilie Chirtoaca, President of the Legal Resources Centre. In a podcast for Radio Free Europe, Chirtoaca spoke about the challenges and risks in the justice reform process and the "arduous" evaluations for the new components of the justice self-administration institutions. He stated that more commitments will be needed, even if negotiations begin, with 35 chapters to be tackled. Chirtoaca suggested that the work is just beginning and Moldova is still on the starting path of justice reform.

 


NEWS FROM TRANSNISTRIAN REGION

 


About 76% of the inhabitants of Transnistrian region hold Moldovan citizenship: Tens of thousands of residents on the left bank of Nistru have regained their Moldovan citizenship in the last five years

Source: ziarulnational.md

Official records in Chisinau show nearly 365,000 Transnistrian region residents, the majority of whom are Moldovan citizens. As per the Bureau for Reintegration (BPR), as of mid-September, 364,986 residents from the left bank of the Nistru River and the city of Tighina were on the population register. Of these, 355,934 held Moldovan citizenship, 334,444 had Moldovan passports, and 298,207 had ID cards. This year, 2,187 Transnistrian residents benefited from facilitated ID card issuance. From 19 April 2018 to 14 September 2023, the BPR recognised 34,090 individuals as Moldovan citizens, with about 69% being residents from the left bank of the Dniester and the city of Bender (Tighina).

Subject: EEAS DELEGATIONS PRESS REVIEW - MOLDOVA - 28 September 2023



 

Daily Press Review

28 September 2023 

EU Delegation Moldova


 
POLITICAL NEWS

 

The explosive part of a rocket that fell into the lake in Harbova , Anenii Noi, was detonated

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

Specialists from Bombteh detonated the explosive component of a rocket that fell into the lake in Harbova village, Anenii Noi district, about 60 kilometres from Chisinau. In order for the intervention to be operated safely, the specialists evacuated the water from the lake. The authorities have confirmed that the debris come from an aerial missile, and specialists will identify its type and origin. The MAI states that there was no danger to the population. The area was isolated, and the first houses are located at a distance of one kilometre. Few days earlier, fragments of a rocket fell in the village of Chitcani in Causeni district.



Spinu: A mayor who is against the EU is a mayor who acts against the development of his locality

Source: realitatea.md

Andrei Spinu, Minister for Infrastructure and Regional Development, asserted on Rlive TV's Rezoomat programme that a mayor against the European Union (EU) acts against their own locality's development. Spinu clarified that government-managed funds reach all localities, irrespective of the mayor's views. Spinu emphasised that without pre-accession or European funds, local development cannot be achieved. He pointed out that the EU will not finance Moldova if the country does not fulfil its EU accession action plans. Drawing on Romania, Bulgaria, and Croatia's experiences, he noted that once certain things are done, resources become available. This emphasises the importance of EU relations for local and national development.



The Revival Party's candidate for the position of Mayor of the capital, Vasile Bolea: connections with Shor, integration into the Customs Union and homophobic comments

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

Ahead of local elections, Vasile Bolea has left the Socialist Party and joined the Revival Party, which is under scrutiny for alleged illegal financing from oligarch Ilan Shor's organised crime group . Bolea, after announcing his candidacy for the position of Mayor of the capital, met with Russian Ambassador Oleg Vasne ov to discuss bilateral issues, regional trends, and local elections. The Revival Party plans to organise a referendum on Moldova's potential membership in the Eurasian Economic Union, Bolea explained. Previously, Bolea protested against the signing of the Association Agreement with the European Union. Meanwhile, the Socialist Party accused the Shor Party of attempting to corrupt socialist deputies and local elected officials in March 2023.


The new Minister of Finance has taken the oath of office

Source: voceabasarabiei.md

The designated Minister of Finance, Petru Rotaru, took the oath of office on 28 September. The ceremony took place in the presence of the President of the Republic of Moldova, Maia Sandu. The head of state thanked the former Minister of Finance, Veronica Sireteanu, who left office for maternal leave, for agreeing to take on "the responsibility of managing the Ministry of Finance in a difficult economic period ". Maia Sandu said that the new minister will lead the institution that oversees the good and prudent use of public money, our money of all, this being a responsible mission". The president also said that the experience of the new Minister of Finance, former head of Tax Office, is valuable for continuing efforts to reduce bureaucracy in the tax and customs fields.


Fugitive oligarch, sanctioned by the EU, filed a complaint against EU Council s decision

Source: jurnal.md

The oligarch Vladimir Plahotniuc, sanctioned in May by the Brussels authorities for attempts to destabilize the Republic of Moldova, sued the Council of the European Union. The case was registered on 9 August, but it was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 25 September. More specifically, Vladimir Plahotniuc requests the Court to cancel the decision regarding the establishment of restrictive measures against him and the annulment of the Regulation implementing the decision. The lawyer representing his interests in this case is Jason Pobjoy, specialized in European law, international law, public, commercial and competition law.


Websites of state institutions and of independent media were subjects to cyber attacks

Source: newsmaker.md

The spokesperson of the Government, Daniel Voda, has said that the websites of Chisinau airport, the energy regulator and the Foreign Ministry have been subjected to "massive DDoS attacks", but the relevant agency managed to minimise their impact. He explained that access to the websites from abroad "was temporarily limited to prevent their takeover". NewsMaker.md and a few other media, including the website of the Ziarul de Garda weekly and the Nokta website, as well as websites of several energy companies reported hacking attacks on 25-26 September.The Russian-language Telegram channel Narodnaya Cyber Armiya (People's Cyber Army) claimed responsibility for for these attacks.

 


ECONOMIC NEWS

 


Romania is interested in buying Moldovan Giurgiulesti international free port on Danube

Source: infotag.md


Romania is interested in buying the Giurgiulesti international free port from the Republic of Moldova. Romanian Prime Minister Marcel Ciolacu told Digi24.ro that the Romanian Minister of Transport has already discussed this topic with a representative of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the sole final owner of the company that manages the Danube port. Ciolacu mentioned that negotiations should not be conducted with the Moldovan authorities, since the shareholder of the Giurgiulesti port is the EBRD and, therefore, the negotiations will be conducted with the bank. Due to the war near the Moldovan border, the port of Giurgiulesti played a key role in the supply of goods to and from Ukraine, reaching a record cargo trans-shipment volume of 1.8 million tons in 2022. At the same time, 62% of goods exported through port were sent to the European Union. In this sense, a new berth is being built in the port of Giurgiulesti, to increase the trans-shipment of goods.

Andrei Spinu's promise: Moldova should get rid of Gazprom"

Source: moldova.europalibera.org

Andrei Spinu, Minister of Infrastructure and Regional Development, has promised to resume the repair of a key road to Tiraspol, left unfinished before the European Political Community summit at Bulboaca in June. Spinu discussed this shortly after launching an ambitious infrastructure reconstruction plan in Moldova, which he presents as a priority in his new term in the PAS government. He acknowledged that the authorities "had to ensure a good road up to the place" of the summit, and confirmed that work on the uncompleted section would resume in 2024 as part of a broader effort to rebuild the roads. Known for his role in solving the gas crisis from 2021-2022, Spinu told Free Europe that "Moldova must no longer have any relationship with Gazprom", the Russian state concern that was for a long time the only supplier of gas to Moldovan consumers.



Moldova's economy, hit by the crisis in 2023. EBRD adjusted the forecast for our country

Source: realitatea.md

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has adjusted its forecast for the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of Moldova for the current year, now anticipating zero economic growth rather than the previously predicted 1.3% decline. This announcement was made in the new regional economic analysis published in September. Meanwhile, the EBRD has maintained its economic growth forecast for Moldova in 2024, expecting the country's GDP to significantly increase by 3.5%. These adjustments follow an assessment of the economic situation in the first half of 2023, marking an improvement in recovery prospects. Despite a 2.4% decline in GDP in the first quarter of 2023, mainly due to the continuous decline in private consumption, there are signs of improvement.

 


FOREIGN POLICY

 


Ambassador: Attracting Chinese investments to Moldova is one of our priorities

Source: realitatea.md

China and Moldova are two friendly nations and great partners, always supporting each other in matters concerning sovereignty and territorial integrity, according to China's ambassador to Moldova, Yan Wenbin. In a speech marking the 74th anniversary of the proclamation of the People's Republic of China, Wenbin highlighted the strong desire to develop cooperation between the two countries in areas such as trade, investment, culture, and tourism. He emphasised that China's vast market is open to high-quality agricultural products from Moldova, and the Chinese Embassy is working to simplify the process for Moldovan sunflower and grape seeds to enter the Chinese market. Additionally, several memorandums of collaboration have been signed between universities in both countries.



Portugal will continue to support Moldova in the European integration process

Source: moldova1.md

Portugal will continue to support Moldova in its European integration process. This was discussed by Moldovan deputies Angela Munteanu-Pojoga and Iulia Dascalu and Portuguese parliamentarians. The officials also discussed trade and economic cooperation, legislative collaboration on anti-corruption measures, identifying and repatriating fraudulent assets, modernising energy infrastructure, and developing agriculture. The deputies also attended a concert organised by the Moldovan Cultural Centre in Portugal, marking its 20th anniversary, and presented the centre's leadership with certificates of high appreciation for their contribution to the Moldovan diaspora and their promotion of Moldovan culture and traditions.

 


EU-MOLDOVA RELATIONS

 


Roberta Metsola hopes that the EU will open accession negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova by the end of the year

Source: moldova1.md

President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola hopes that the EU will open accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova by year-end, asking for the hopes of these candidate countries not to be disappointed. Instead of focusing on a target date, Metsola stressed the importance of initiating accession negotiations by the end of the year. She has always shown her support for Ukraine's EU accession, even visiting Kyiv in April 2022 after the Russian invasion began. The EU granted Ukraine and Moldova candidate status in June 2022, although denied this to Georgia, calling for more reforms. The next step, opening accession negotiations, requires the fulfilment of seven benchmarks defined by the European Commission, mainly concerning widespread corruption and judicial reform.

With just over two months until Brussels' decision on the prospect of opening Moldova's EU accession negotiations, up to 80% of justice commitments, six out of nine, have been fulfilled, according to Ilie Chirtoaca, President of the Legal Resources Centre. In a podcast for Radio Free Europe, Chirtoaca spoke about the challenges and risks in the justice reform process and the "arduous" evaluations for the new components of the justice self-administration institutions. About 76% of the inhabitants of Transnistrian region hold Moldovan citizenship: Tens of thousands of residents on the left bank of Nistru have regained their Moldovan citizenship in the last five years

Source: ziarulnational.md

Official records in Chisinau show nearly 365,000 Transnistrian region residents, the majority of whom are Moldovan citizens. As per the Bureau for Reintegration (BPR), as of mid-September, 364,986 residents from the left bank of the Nistru River and the city of Tighina were on the population register. Of these, 355,934 held Moldovan citizenship, 334,444 had Moldovan passports, and 298,207 had ID cards. This year, 2,187 Transnistrian residents benefited from facilitated ID card issuance. From 19 April 2018 to 14 September 2023, the BPR recognised 34,090 individuals as Moldovan citizens, with about 69% being residents from the left bank of the Dniester and the city of Bender (Tighina).
